scope: unit-contexts-v1 (24 contexts) under public rules r4; written before any r4 or pilot-v2.1 output existed
policy: A context is 'ambiguous' when its scoring reference (the exact evidence posterior under the dev-v2 generator) depends on generator knowledge that neither the r4 rules nor the visible history give the model, in a way that moves a defensible value across the SUPPORT_MIN = 0.2 threshold. In ambiguous contexts an answer whose posterior is < 0.2 is scored 'ambiguous_reference' (reported apart, never counted as a model error); answers with posterior >= 0.2 are scored normally. Primary category counts use the non-ambiguous contexts.

uc01.basis: Remark 'I saw <recipient> head to the office' implies the speaker holds an office belief; the robot cannot tell which office (0.5/0.5). A reader might put a little mass on the remark being inaccurate, but the support set {offices} is what the remark implies.

uc02.basis: K(recipient) rests only on one claim by a speaker who states an incentive; the 0.95/0.05 split is the generator's accuracy base rate for such claimants. The other office is publicly defensible but scores < 0.2.

uc03.basis: Speaker states the value; honest-claimant base rate undisclosed, but the top value is the stated one.

uc04.basis: Rule 2 (recipient knows own start location); robot cannot tell which office: both offices supported. Undisclosed under r3.

uc05.basis: Rule 2, as uc04. Undisclosed under r3.

uc06.basis: K(claimant with stated incentive): whether she believes her own claim is the generator's base rate (0.975/0.025). The other value is publicly defensible but scores < 0.2.

uc07.basis: Two people state conflicting values; which one is accurate (0.867/0.133) comes from the generator's role assignment, not visible evidence. The minority value scores < 0.2.

uc08.basis: '<j> told me this morning where the meeting is' implies j holds a meeting-room belief; offices 0.5/0.5.

uc09.basis: Speaker saw the recipient head to an office; offices 0.5/0.5.

uc10.basis: R(j->k): the assessment comes from a hidden vouch/warn backstory template; no visible statement links j's view to k (they are co-present, k states an incentive, and j answers the robot's location question).

uc11.basis: R(j->k): the two people are only co-present, with k's incentive remark; no visible statement links j's view to k. The assessment comes from a hidden vouch/warn backstory template, and the posterior excludes 'unknown' only because the template always gives j an assessment. r4 rule 1's 'neither saw nor was told' is phrased about facts, so it points to 'unknown' only by a loose reading.

uc12.basis: R(j) intent of a person with a stated incentive; both intents supported (0.5/0.5).

uc14.basis: Rule 5: seeing someone gives no belief about their belief -> unknown. Conflicted with the r3 wording.

uc15.basis: Rule 5: j told k before the task -> j thinks k believes it; offices 0.5/0.5.

uc16.basis: Rule 4: ordinary remarks create no beliefs about beliefs -> unknown. Conflicted with the r3 wording.

uc17.basis: Rule 5: no statement between the two people -> unknown.

uc18.basis: Rule 5: co-witnessing gives no belief about the other's belief -> unknown.

uc19.basis: Rule 5, last sentence: an in-task statement gives the speaker no belief about listeners -> unknown.

uc20.basis: Speaker stated the value and reported seeing it.

uc21.basis: Rule 2 plus a statement of the recipient's location. Undisclosed under r3.

uc23.basis: 'I was out of the building all morning' -> saw nothing -> unknown.

uc24.basis: Rule 2; robot cannot tell which office.

wording_revisions: 2026-10-28, after the Sonnet facts check and after Round 1 local outputs existed: basis wording of uc01, uc10, uc11 made accurate; no flag changed.
